Diagnostic

Il est clinique.

  • Inflammation du bord libre de la paupière.
  • Localisations :
    • blépharite antérieure : au niveau de la région d'implantation des cils,
    • blépharite postérieure : en arrière des cils (associé à un dysfonctionnement des glandes de Meibomius),
    • blépharite mixte : inflammation des territoires antérieur et postérieur.
  • Signes fonctionnels (non spécifiques) :
    • sensation de sécheresse oculaire,
    • irritation,
    • larmoiement,
    • sensation de brûlure,
    • photophobie,
    • vision floue,
  • Examen des paupières :
    • irritation du bord libre de la paupière,
    • croûtes ou collerettes du bord libre de la paupière,
    • télangiectasies importantes du bord libre de la paupière,
    • œdème conjonctival autour des méats des glandes de Meibomius,
    • bouchons de kératine à l'abouchement des glandes de Meibomius,
    • anomalies du bord libre : chalazions, voussures, irrégularité (cratères),
    • perte de cils et ulcères +/- orgelets associés,
  • Examen oculaire :
    • rougeur oculaire,
    • larmes d'aspect mousseux et bulleux au niveau du bord libre (meiborrhée),
    • cornée :
      • kératite ponctuée inférieure, sous forme d'ulcères ou de phlyctènes (rare),
      • cicatrices cornéennes localisées au niveau limbique inférieur, néovascularisées,
    • conjonctivite papillaire chronique, +/- fibrose sous-conjonctivale.
  • Pression d'une glande pour analyser l'aspect du meibum : 
    • normal : huileux, sort facilement à la pression,
    • meibomite : aspect visqueux et trouble, sort difficilement,
    • atrophie meibomienne : absence totale de meibum à la pression.
  • Si test de rupture du film lacrymal réalisé : temps de rupture diminué.
Principales étiologies
  • Dysfonctionnement des glandes de Meibomius :
    • agénésie congénitale,
    • pathologie dermatologique :
      • rosacée (voir fiche),
      • dermite séborrhéique (voir fiche),
      • atopie (voir fiche),
      • psoriasis (voir fiche),
    • séquelle d'une pathologie cicatricielle :
      • trachome,
      • pemphigoïde,
      • Lyell,
    • iatrogénie : rétinoïdes,
    • irritation (cosmétiques),
    • néoplasie,
    • autres causes.
  • Infection :
    • à germes cutanés (surtout staphylocoques),
    • à Demodex (croûtes grasses formant un manchon autour de la base des cils).
Prise en charge
  • Très faible niveau de preuve des traitements proposés.
  • Éducation (version imprimable).
  • Phase aiguë (traitement durant au moins 6 semaines) :
    • hygiène douce des paupières avec une compresse pour retirer les débris (éviter les massages vigoureux et les contacts avec la surface oculaire),
    • fluidification du meibum par application pluriquotidienne (2 à 4 fois par jour à la phase aiguë puis de façon plus espacée) pendant 5 à 10 minutes de :
      • compresses humidifiées à l'eau modérément chaude  (en réchauffant périodiquement la compresse à mesure qu'elle refroidit), ou
      • masque oculaire chauffant (nombreux modèles disponibles dans le commerce, sans preuve de supériorité sur les compresses chaudes mais dont le maniement peut sembler plus pratique à certains patients),
    • massage des paupières immédiatement après l'application des compresses chaudes pour drainer les glandes de Meibomius,
    • larmes artificielles en cas de sécheresse oculaire (voir fiche),
    • élimination d'éventuels facteurs déclenchant/favorisant identifiés.
  • En cas de retentissement sur la vision ou sur la qualité de vie : avis spécialisé rapide.
  • En cas d'échec du traitement et de symptômes modérés : avis spécialisé sans urgence.

L70: L71: Blepharitis is inflammation of the rims of the eyelids, which causes them to become red and swollen. It is a common condition which can develop at any age but is more common in young children and people over 50. Most people experience repeated episodes followed by periods with no symptoms. It is not possible to catch blepharitis from someone else who has it. L72: ## What are the symptoms of blepharitis? L73: L74: Many people with the condition experience the symptoms of blepharitis in repeated episodes, with the symptoms coming and going. Blepharitis symptoms can include: L75: L76: * Soreness and swelling of the eyelids L77: * A stinging, burning or gritty sensation in the eyes L78: * Itchy eyes and eyelids L79: * Red eyes and eyelids L80: * Crustiness and flakiness of the skin around the eyelash root L81: * Sticking of the eyelids when waking up L82: Blepharitis may also cause sensitivity to light, increased frequency of blinking and may lead to the development of chalazions on the eyelid. Those who experience blepharitis may also experience a dry eye condition where not enough tears are produced. L83: Although not usually serious, blepharitis can be uncomfortable, so wearing contact lenses and applying eye makeup should be avoided when you have symptoms. It’s important to seek treatment for blepharitis as soon as possible to alleviate the symptoms and reduce the risk of other conditions developing. L84: ## What causes blepharitis? L85: There is no direct cause of blepharitis but it is more common in people who have skin conditions such as eczema and acne, and in those with allergic diseases like asthma. Eyelids contain tiny glands that make an oil which keeps the eyes moist as part of the tear film. In blepharitis, these glands become blocked, which causes irritated eyelids and dry, sore eyes. It is thought that in some people, blepharitis is partly caused by sensitivity to the bacteria (staphylococcus) which normally live on the skin. L86: ### Blepharitis treatment is available at Moorfields Private L87: L88: You can self-fund or use private medical insurance to fund your treatment. It's not usually serious and can often be treated by washing your eyelids every day. L16: ## Symptoms of blepharitis L17: L18: Blepharitis symptoms often come and go. L19: L20: Symptoms of blepharitis include: L21: L22: * sore eyelids L23: * itchy eyes L24: * a gritty feeling in the eyes L25: * flakes or crusts around the roots of the eyelashes L26: * eyelids sticking together in the morning when you wake up L27: 【6†Image: Blepharitis in someone with white skin. MARAZZI/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY https://www.sciencephoto.com/media/256626/view L31: L32: Information: L33: ### If you're not sure it's blepharitis L34: L35: 【7†Find out more about eyelid problems】 L36: L37: ## Things you can do to treat and prevent blepharitis L38: L39: ### Do L40: L41: * clean your eyelids twice a day L42: L43: * continue to clean your eyes, even if your symptoms clear up L44: L45: ### Don’t L46: L47: * do not wear contact lenses while you have symptoms L48: L49: * do not use eye makeup, especially eyeliner and mascara, while you have symptoms L50: ### How to clean your eyes L51: L52: 1. Soak a clean flannel or cotton wool in warm water and place it on your closed eyelid for 5 to 10 minutes. L53: 2. Gently massage your eyelids for around 30 seconds. L54: 3. Clean your eyelids using cotton wool or a cotton bud. It might help to use a small amount of baby shampoo in water. Gently wipe along the edge of your eyelids to remove any flakes or crusts. L55: ### A pharmacist can help with blepharitis L56: L57: A pharmacist might be able to suggest things to help keep your eyelids clean, including: L58: L59: * eye pads and wipes L60: * eyedrops L61: 【8†Find a pharmacy】 L62: L63: ## Non-urgent advice: See a GP if: L64: L65: * blepharitis symptoms do not improve, or get worse L66: ## Treatment for blepharitis from a GP L67: L68: A GP might suggest using an antibiotic cream or ointment that you rub on your eyelid if your blepharitis does not clear up after cleaning your eyelids regularly. L69: L70: If blepharitis has caused other problems, such as a lump of fluid under the skin (cyst), antibiotic eyedrops or tablets may be recommended. L71: L72: If your blepharitis is severe, or if you also have other eye symptoms, the GP may refer you to an eye specialist (ophthalmologist). L73: ## Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if you have: L74: L75: * pain in your eyes L76: * changes to your vision, such as vision loss or blurred vision L77: * very red eyes L78: L79: These can be signs of a more serious eye problem. L80: L81: You can call 111 or 【9†get help from 111 online†111.nhs.uk】. L82: ## Causes of blepharitis L83: L84: Blepharitis can be caused by: L85: L86: * a type of bacteria that lives on the skin L87: * a skin condition, such as seborrhoeic dermatitis L88: * the glands inside the eyelids not producing enough oil L89: L90: Blepharitis cannot be spread to other people.
